singlePointsOfFailure.description: The legacy-auth-cluster is a single point of failure as it is the only system mentioned for recovery.
singlePointsOfFailure.mitigationSuggestion: Identify and implement a backup plan for the legacy-auth-cluster to ensure it is not a single point of failure.

gapAnalysis.description: Step(s) 1, 2, 3, 4 have no validation command to confirm they succeeded.
gapAnalysis.recommendation: Add a concrete validation command or check to each recovery step.

gapAnalysis.description: No step describes how to roll back or revert the recovery procedure if it fails partway through.
gapAnalysis.recommendation: Add explicit rollback steps for at least the highest-risk actions.

gapAnalysis.description: The action for step 2 is to 'Rotate the session-signing keys in old-secrets-vault (deprecated, replaced by vault-v2 but never migrated).'
gapAnalysis.recommendation: Clarify the steps for rotating session-signing keys, including the specific commands and any prerequisites.

gapAnalysis.description: The action for step 3 is to 'Rebuild the auth-token-cache from the legacy-auth-cluster snapshot.'
gapAnalysis.recommendation: Specify the steps for rebuilding the auth-token-cache, including the specific commands and any prerequisites.

suggestions.title: Add Validation Commands
suggestions.detail: Add validation commands for each step to ensure they are executed successfully.

suggestions.title: Implement Rollback Steps
suggestions.detail: Add explicit rollback steps for the highest-risk actions to ensure recovery can be attempted again if necessary.

suggestions.title: Identify and Address Single Points of Failure
suggestions.detail: Identify and implement backup plans for single points of failure, such as the legacy-auth-cluster.

suggestions.title: Clarify Vague Instructions
suggestions.detail: Clarify the steps for rotating session-signing keys and rebuilding the auth-token-cache to ensure they are clear and actionable.

suggestions.title: Review RTO and RPO
suggestions.detail: Review the RTO and RPO to ensure they are realistic and achievable, and adjust if necessary.

summary: The DR runbook for the Auth Service outlines steps to recover from a failure, but lacks validation commands and explicit rollback steps. The runbook is focused on manual steps and does not cover potential single points of failure or dependencies. The Recovery Time Objective (RTO) is met, but the Recovery Point Objective (RPO) is not, indicating a need for more robust recovery procedures.
